config.title: Holy grail layout

intro.title: Holy grail layout
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a classic 'holy grail' webpage layout, which includes a header, footer, a main content area, and two sidebars. You will learn how to use CSS Grid to create this responsive, multi-column design efficiently. The main technologies involved are CSS Grid properties like grid-template-areas, grid-template-columns, and grid-area for placement. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a complex layout with clean, maintainable CSS code.
intro.usecase: The holy grail layout is a foundational pattern used in countless real-world applications where content needs to be organized into distinct, persistent sections. You'll see it implemented in content management systems like WordPress dashboards, which feature a fixed header, sidebar navigation, main content area, and footer. E-commerce platforms like Shopify use this layout for their admin interfaces, keeping tools accessible while displaying product data centrally. News websites and blogs frequently employ this structure to maintain navigation and branding while showcasing articles. As a developer, you'll use this pattern whenever building dashboards, admin panels, documentation sites, or any application requiring consistent spatial organization of UI components.

objectives: Construct a basic HTML structure with header, footer, main content, and two sidebars.
Apply CSS Grid to define a holy grail layout template.
Configure grid areas to position header, footer, main content, and sidebars.
Implement responsive behavior using media queries to adjust the layout.
Manipulate grid column and row sizing to control content dimensions.
Integrate flexbox within grid items for internal alignment.
Update the layout to handle varying content heights dynamically.

steps.title: Create the basic HTML structure for holy grail layout
steps.instruction: Create a container div with header, main, left sidebar, right sidebar, and footer elements inside.
steps.hint: Use HTML element tags inside a div container. The structure should include: header, main, aside (for sidebars), and footer.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Basic HTML structure example */
Header
Left Sidebar
Main Content
Right Sidebar
Footer
steps.seedCode: /* Create your holy grail HTML structure here */
steps.expectedOutcome: A complete HTML structure with container, header, main content area, two sidebars, and footer elements.
successCriteria: The code contains a div container with header, main, two aside elements (or similar), and footer elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some elements, but make sure to include all required parts: container, header, main, left sidebar, right sidebar, and footer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure is incomplete or incorrect. Review the holy grail layout requirements and try again.

steps.title: Apply basic reset and box-sizing
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule using the universal selector (*) to set margin and padding to 0, and box-sizing to border-box.
steps.hint: The universal selector targets all elements. Use the box-sizing property with border-box value to include padding and border in element width/height.
steps.expectedOutcome: A universal selector rule that resets margins and paddings to zero and sets box-sizing to border-box.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a universal selector rule with margin: 0, padding: 0, and box-sizing: border-box properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your universal selector rule includes all three properties: margin: 0, padding: 0, and box-sizing: border-box.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the expected CSS reset. Try using the universal selector (*) with margin: 0, padding: 0, and box-sizing: border-box properties.

steps.title: Style the container with flexbox
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for a container class that sets display to flex and flex-direction to column.
steps.hint: Use .container selector with display: flex; and flex-direction: column; properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container class will be styled as a flex container with column direction.
successCriteria: CSS rule for .container exists with display: flex and flex-direction: column properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your .container rule includes both display: flex and flex-direction: column.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container styling is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the correct selector and properties.

steps.title: Style the header and footer
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the header and footer elements. Give them a height of 80px, a background color of #333, and center-align their text with white color.
steps.hint: You can use the element selectors 'header' and 'footer' to target them. Set the height, background-color, color, and text-align properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The header and footer will have a dark background, fixed height, and centered white text.
successCriteria: The CSS includes rules for both header and footer with height: 80px, background-color: #333, color: white, and text-align: center.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both header and footer have all four required properties: height, background-color, color, and text-align.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header and footer are not styled correctly. Check that you've added CSS rules for both elements with the specified properties.

steps.title: Create the main content area with flexbox
steps.instruction: Style the main element to use flexbox and fill the available space between the header and footer.
steps.hint: Set display: flex on the main element and use flex-grow: 1 to make it expand.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main element will be styled as a flex container that grows to fill the vertical space.
successCriteria: The main element has display: flex and flex-grow: 1 applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both display: flex and flex-grow: 1 to the main element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main element is not properly styled as a flex container. Check the CSS properties.

steps.title: Style the left and right sidebars
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the left and right sidebar elements with fixed widths and background colors.
steps.hint: Use the element selectors for the sidebar elements and set width and background-color properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The left and right sidebar elements will have defined widths and background colors.
successCriteria: CSS rules for both sidebar elements with width and background-color properties are added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both sidebar elements have width and background-color properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sidebars aren't styled yet. Add CSS rules for the sidebar elements with width and background-color properties.

steps.title: Style the main content area
steps.instruction: Apply flex-grow to the main content area and add padding for spacing.
steps.hint: Use the flex-grow property to make the main content take up remaining space, and add padding for internal spacing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main content area will expand to fill available space and have comfortable internal spacing.
successCriteria: The main content area has flex-grow: 1 and padding applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to include both flex-grow and padding properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main content area styling is incomplete or incorrect. Review the flex-grow and padding properties.

steps.title: Add responsive design with media queries
steps.instruction: Add a media query that stacks the sidebars vertically on screens narrower than 768px.
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 768px) to target smaller screens, then adjust the flex-direction of .main-content to column.
steps.expectedOutcome: The layout will adapt to mobile screens by stacking sidebars vertically.
successCriteria: A media query with max-width: 768px changes .main-content flex-direction to column.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the media query targets .main-content and sets flex-direction: column.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query is missing or incorrect. Try using @media (max-width: 768px) { .main-content { flex-direction: column; } }.

steps.title: Enhance visual styling with colors and spacing
steps.instruction: Add contrasting background colors and consistent padding to the left and right sidebars to improve visual hierarchy.
steps.hint: Use the background-color property with different colors for each sidebar, and adjust the padding values to create balanced spacing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The left and right sidebars will have distinct background colors and balanced padding, making the layout more visually appealing.
successCriteria: The left-sidebar and right-sidebar selectors have different background-color values and consistent padding values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both sidebars have distinct background colors and balanced padding values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sidebars don't have the expected styling. Check that you've added background-color and padding properties to both sidebar selectors.

steps.title: Add final polish and test the layout
steps.instruction: Add sample content inside each layout section to test the holy grail layout's structure and responsiveness.
steps.hint: Add placeholder text or simple content like headings and paragraphs inside the header, footer, sidebars, and main content area.
steps.expectedOutcome: The holy grail layout will have visible sample content in all sections, making it easier to verify the structure works correctly.
successCriteria: Sample content is added to header, footer, left sidebar, right sidebar, and main content area.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some test content, but make sure to include content in all sections: header, footer, both sidebars, and main content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The layout sections still lack test content. Add sample text or elements to each section to test the structure.
